verdict_summary: ACCEPT. This closes the one gap from round 1. A new committed test in materials.test.ts constructs a PodmanRunner subclass (HandoverProbe) that reaches the private handOverMaterials method without widening its production visibility, and - critically - configures the runner's podman binary as a path that cannot execute, so if any guard clause were removed the test would fail with a spawn error rather than pass silently: reaching podman at all is itself proof the guard fired first. Four cases are covered: a missing directory, a regular file in its place, a symlink to a good directory (with an added assertion that the symlink's target was never chmodded, proving no side effect leaked through before the refusal), and a directory the runner does not own. A second new test in podman.integration.test.ts proves the same guarantee through the real start() path: materials: '/' is refused with the typed error, no container carries the worker's name afterwards (checked via podman ps -a --filter), and the filesystem root is untouched. tasks/factory/w01d-GATES.md's G3 now cites real CHECK commands and receipts like every other gate, and explicitly credits the finding: 'The validator found these three branches untested, which was correct.' All static gates, the materials unit suite, and the full shared Podman suite pass at this exact head; the coverage gates pass cleanly with my own merged LCOV.

g3_fix_verification.satisfies_this_round's_explicit_requirem: the team lead asked that 'the tests would fail if the guard were removed' - the unusable podman binary path is exactly the mechanism that makes this true: removing any of the three guard clauses would let handOverMaterials reach `command(this.podman, [...])`, which would then fail with a spawn error (ENOENT) rather than the expected RunnerError, failing the test's `.code`/`.message` assertions
